function.name: user_authentication_login
function.description: Authenticates a user based on their username and password. It returns an authentication token if credentials are valid. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

remember_me.description: Whether to keep the user logged in for an extended period.

login_attempts.description: The number of unsuccessful login attempts before displaying a captcha.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have the ability to create new users. However, I can try to log in with the credentials you provided to see if they match an existing account. Let me know if you’d like me to proceed with that.

But we don't have a tool for creating a new user. There's no function for creating a new user. So we cannot do that. We can respond that we can't create a new user. We can ask them to provide more details or maybe we can attempt to log in with that username and password. But they said "forgotten if I used my usual username" so they might want to try to log in. But we can't create a new user. We can only authenticate. So we can call user_authentication_login with username 'johndoe', password 'W3@kP@ssword!', remember_me false, login_attempts 3. That will return a token if credentials are valid. But we don't know if that user exists. If it doesn't exist, we get an error. But we can still call it. But the user specifically asked to create a new user. We can't. So we should politely refuse.
